title: Book of Moses 1:33–38
speaker: Joseph Smith
venue: Revelation (Visions of Moses), later canonized in the Pearl of Great Price
summary: God's creative work is presented as endless: worlds without number have been created, and as one earth passes away another comes.
transcription: And worlds without number have I created; and I also created them for mine own purpose... The heavens, they are many, and they cannot be numbered unto man; but they are numbered unto me, for they are mine. And as one earth shall pass away, and the heavens thereof even so shall another come; and there is no end to my works, neither to my words.
notes: Earliest canonical statement of an unending cosmological process. Chain language here is about worlds, not Gods — but it supplies the scaffolding later regress teachings build on.

title: Book of Abraham 3:18–26; 4:1
speaker: Joseph Smith
venue: Published in Times and Seasons, Nauvoo; later canonized in the Pearl of Great Price
summary: Intelligences (spirits) 'have no beginning... no end'; a plurality of Gods ('the Gods') organize the heavens and the earth.
transcription: If there be two spirits, and one shall be more intelligent than the other... they shall have no beginning; they existed before, they shall have no end, they shall exist after, for they are gnolaum, or eternal... And then the Lord said: Let us go down. And they went down at the beginning, and they, that is the Gods, organized and formed the heavens and the earth.
notes: The tripartite framework's proof text: eternal, uncreated intelligences plus 'the Gods' as organizers rather than creators ex nihilo. In tension with later viviparous readings that make spirits literal offspring with a birth-point.

title: Doctrine and Covenants 132:19–20, 63
speaker: Joseph Smith
venue: Revelation recorded at Nauvoo; first published 1852; canonized 1876
summary: Those sealed and exalted 'shall be gods' with 'a continuation of the seeds forever and ever' — the canonical anchor for eternal increase.
transcription: ...they shall pass by the angels, and the gods, which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods, because they have no end; therefore shall they be from everlasting to everlasting, because they continue; then shall they be above all, because all things are subject unto them... they are ordained to bear the souls of men; for herein is the work of my Father continued, that he may be glorified.
notes: The load-bearing canonical text for forward progression. 'Continuation of the seeds' is the phrase every later euphemism orbits — compare Oaks 2019, which quotes it while leaving the referent unstated.

title: King Follett Discourse
speaker: Joseph Smith
summary: God 'was once as we are now, and is an exalted man'; the mind of man is co-eternal with God — spirits were not created but are self-existent.
transcription: God himself was once as we are now, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens!... you have got to learn how to be Gods yourselves, and to be kings and priests to God, the same as all Gods have done before you... The mind or the intelligence which man possesses is co-equal [co-eternal] with God himself... God never had the power to create the spirit of man at all. God himself could not create himself. Intelligence is eternal and exists upon a self-existent principle.
notes: Amalgamated from contemporaneous notes by Bullock, Clayton, Richards, and Woodruff — hence B, not A. Republished in the Ensign, April/May 1971, and quoted in Teachings of Presidents: Joseph Smith (2007). The co-eternal-intelligence passage is the strongest support for the adoption/organization reading of spirit origins, against viviparous spirit birth. Individual scribal accounts: Joseph Smith Papers, 'Discourse, 7 April 1844.'

title: Sermon in the Grove
speaker: Joseph Smith
venue: East grove near the temple, Nauvoo
summary: Commenting on Revelation 1:6, Joseph Smith teaches explicitly that God the Father himself had a Father — the clearest backward-regress statement in his corpus.
transcription: If Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and John discovered that God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father, you may suppose that He had a Father also. Where was there ever a son without a father?... Hence if Jesus had a Father, can we not believe that He had a Father also? I despise the idea of being scared to death at such a doctrine, for the Bible is full of it.
notes: Text as printed in History of the Church 6:473–79 and Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith 370–73, amalgamated from the Bullock and Clayton reports — link goes to the Joseph Smith Papers Bullock account for hearsay transparency. This is the passage the 2018 New Testament institute manual still quotes (see the ch. 53 entry), making it the lone explicit backward regress surviving in a current manual.

title: Lorenzo Snow couplet
speaker: Lorenzo Snow
venue: Private epiphany, Nauvoo; published and reaffirmed repeatedly thereafter
summary: 'As man now is, God once was; as God now is, man may be' — the couplet that compresses both directions of the doctrine into a single sentence.
transcription: As man now is, God once was: As God now is, man may be.
notes: Rated A rather than C: although the 1840 origin story is later recollection, Snow personally reaffirmed the couplet in print many times as an apostle and president, and Teachings of Presidents: Lorenzo Snow ch. 5 (2012) republishes it — a current-correlated source. The Gospel Topics essay 'Becoming Like God' (2014) engages the couplet's second half while going quiet on the first.

title: Brigham Young on the endless chain of Gods — and his caution
speaker: Brigham Young
venue: Tabernacle discourses, Salt Lake City (Journal of Discourses)
summary: Young taught an endless succession of Gods ('How many Gods there are, I do not know. But there never was a time when there were not Gods') while discouraging inquiry into 'the origin of Gods.'
transcription: How many Gods there are, I do not know. But there never was a time when there were not Gods and worlds, and when men were not passing through the same ordeals that we are now passing through. That course has been from all eternity, and it is and will be to all eternity. (JD 7:333) ... It is the height of folly for men to try to find out the origin of the Gods.
notes: Rated E for the Journal of Discourses attribution chain (shorthand reports, edited for publication; some discourses B-grade where Watt's shorthand survives). The 1997 manual Teachings of Presidents: Brigham Young republishes the caution — verify the exact chapter ('Knowing and Honoring the Godhead') and quote wording against the manual text. The pairing matters: the same speaker holds the most explicit chain language and the earliest official discouragement of the regress question.

title: Orson Pratt, The Seer
speaker: Orson Pratt
summary: The most systematic viviparous spirit-birth theology ever published by an apostle: spirits literally begotten and born of Heavenly Parents, described in physiological detail.
transcription: Each God, through his wife or wives, raises up a numerous family of sons and daughters... As soon as each God has begotten many millions of male and female spirits... he, in connection with his sons, organizes a new world... The Father of our spirits has only been doing that which His progenitors did before Him.
notes: A-tier hearsay (Pratt's own pen) but never-official — and formally repudiated in part: the First Presidency under Brigham Young publicly disavowed portions of The Seer in 1865, an early RETREAT data point worth its own future entry. Pratt's systematization is the high-water mark the correlated era slowly walks back from.

title: Eliza R. Snow, 'O My Father' ('My Father in Heaven')
speaker: Eliza R. Snow
office: Secretary, Female Relief Society of Nauvoo
venue: Poem published in Times and Seasons; hymn in continuous use since
summary: Canonized-adjacent affirmation of a Mother in Heaven: 'Truth eternal tells me I've a mother there.'
transcription: In the heav'ns are parents single? No, the thought makes reason stare! Truth is reason; truth eternal Tells me I've a mother there. When I leave this frail existence, When I lay this mortal by, Father, Mother, may I meet you In your royal courts on high?
notes: The hymn has anchored Heavenly Mother in lived Latter-day Saint worship for 180 years while the mechanism of spirit generation went unstated — the template for FORWARD-EUPHEMISM avant la lettre. Verify inclusion and hymn number in the new hymnal rollout ('Hymns — For Home and Church,' 2024–), since the print 1985 hymnal (no. 292) is being superseded.

title: First Presidency, 'The Origin of Man'
speaker: Joseph F. Smith, John R. Winder, Anthon H. Lund (First Presidency)
summary: Official First Presidency doctrine: 'man, as a spirit, was begotten and born of heavenly parents' before mortality.
transcription: All men and women are in the similitude of the universal Father and Mother, and are literally the sons and daughters of Deity... man, as a spirit, was begotten and born of heavenly parents, and reared to maturity in the eternal mansions of the Father, prior to coming upon the earth in a temporal body.
notes: The strongest A-tier viviparous statement: first-person First Presidency text, published under their direction. The Ensign reprinted it in full in February 2002 — that reprint is itself a correlation-era data point, since it postdates the Hinckley interviews by five years.

title: First Presidency and the Twelve, 'The Father and the Son: A Doctrinal Exposition'
speaker: First Presidency and Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
summary: Clarifies Elohim/Jehovah usage; Elohim is 'the literal Parent' of Jesus Christ and 'of the spirits of the human race.'
transcription: God the Eternal Father, whom we designate by the exalted name-title 'Elohim,' is the literal Parent of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and of the spirits of the human race.
notes: Reprinted in the Ensign, April 2002, alongside the February 2002 reprint of 'The Origin of Man' — the pair of reprints reads as a quiet reaffirmation of literal spirit parentage at the very moment public-facing rhetoric was softening.

title: Melvin J. Ballard, 'The Sacramental Covenant' / Sermons and Missionary Services
speaker: Melvin J. Ballard
venue: Sermons and Missionary Services of Melvin Joseph Ballard (Bookcraft, 1949)
summary: Spirit bodies described in physiological terms — spirit as literal substance transmitted from Heavenly Parents — with exalted couples promised the same generative power.
transcription: What do we mean by endless or eternal increase? We mean that through the righteousness and faithfulness of men and women who keep the commandments of God they will come forth with celestial bodies, fitted and prepared to enter into their great, high and eternal glory in the celestial kingdom of God, and unto them, through their preparation, there will come spirit children.
notes: The URL points at the 2003 Eternal Marriage Student Manual's 'Eternal Increase' section, which republishes Ballard — see that entry for the correlation significance. Verify the exact excerpt wording against the manual, which trims the 1949 text.

title: The Family: A Proclamation to the World
speaker: First Presidency and Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General Relief Society Meeting; official proclamation
summary: 'Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents' — literal parentage affirmed, mechanism unstated.
transcription: All human beings—male and female—are created in the image of God. Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents, and, as such, each has a divine nature and destiny. Gender is an essential characteristic of individual premortal, mortal, and eternal identity and purpose.
notes: SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS is tagged as implied, not stated: 'spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents' presumes literal parentage without describing generation. The mormonr research page on the proclamation's drafting history is useful background.

title: Gordon B. Hinckley press interviews (Time; San Francisco Chronicle)
speaker: Gordon B. Hinckley
summary: Asked whether God was once a man, Hinckley responds: 'I don't know that we teach it. I don't know that we emphasize it' — the landmark public retreat.
transcription: On whether his church still holds that God the Father was once a man: 'I don't know that we teach it. I don't know that we emphasize it... I understand the philosophical background behind it. But I don't know a lot about it and I don't know that others know a lot about it.' (Time, Aug. 4, 1997) — 'I wouldn't say that. There was a little couplet coined, "As man is, God once was. As God is, man may become." Now that's more of a couplet than anything else.' (San Francisco Chronicle, Apr. 13, 1997)
notes: Never-official: press-interview transcripts, not Church publications — but A-tier as first-person published statements. Compare his October 1997 General Conference response to the coverage: 'I think I understand thoroughly the doctrine of the Church' — an internal reassurance paired with external minimization. The clearest single hinge point of the taper.

title: Eternal Marriage Student Manual, 'Eternal Increase'
speaker: Church Educational System
summary: Republishes Melvin J. Ballard's viviparous spirit-birth teaching under the heading 'Eternal Increase' — the last explicitly viviparous correlated publication.
transcription: See the Ballard 1949 entry for the core excerpt; the manual gathers Ballard, Joseph Fielding Smith, and others under 'Eternal Increase,' teaching that exalted couples will have 'spirit children' and 'eternal increase.'
notes: Still hosted on churchofjesuschrist.org as of 2026, hence current-correlated — but institute curriculum has moved to newer courses, so its practical circulation is residual. As the terminus of explicit viviparism in correlated print, it is the baseline against which the 2014→2025 seminary-manual comparison should be read.

speaker: Church Educational System
summary: Teaches that exalted beings become 'parents of spirit offspring' whose children pass through the same stages of progression.

title: New Testament Student Manual, ch. 53 (Revelation 1–3)
speaker: Church Educational System
summary: Republishes Joseph Smith's Sermon-in-the-Grove commentary on Revelation 1:6 — 'God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father' — the lone explicit backward regress in a current manual.
transcription: The manual quotes Joseph Smith: 'If Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and... God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father, you may suppose that He had a Father also... Hence if Jesus had a Father, can we not believe that He had a Father also?'
notes: A-tier as a manual quoting a B-tier sermon (Bullock/Clayton reports via Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith). Its survival in current curriculum is the strongest counterevidence to a claim that backward regress has been fully retired — and its isolation is equally telling.

title: Gospel Topics Essay, 'Becoming Like God'
speaker: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (unsigned; First Presidency–approved)
summary: Engages the Snow couplet and King Follett Discourse but declines to affirm backward regress ('little has been revealed'), reframing deification through patristic theosis.
transcription: Since human conceptions of reality are necessarily limited in mortality, religions struggle to adequately articulate their visions of eternal glory... Latter-day Saints' doctrine of exaltation is often similarly reduced in media to a cartoonish image of people receiving their own planets... Little has been revealed about the first half of this couplet, and consequently little is taught.
notes: The essay's method is the taper in miniature: quote the historic teaching accurately, then bracket it as unelaborated. The pivot to Irenaeus and C.S. Lewis relocates deification into ecumenical territory where neither regress nor spirit birth needs defending. Verify the 'cartoonish image' and 'little has been revealed' excerpts against the current essay text, which has been lightly revised since 2014.

title: Gospel Topics Essay, 'Mother in Heaven'
speaker: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (unsigned; First Presidency–approved)
summary: Affirms a Heavenly Mother as 'cherished and distinctive' doctrine while remaining silent on the mechanism of spirit generation.
transcription: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints teaches that all human beings, male and female, are beloved spirit children of heavenly parents, a Heavenly Father and a Heavenly Mother. This understanding is rooted in scriptural and prophetic teachings about the nature of God, our relationship to Deity, and the godly potential of men and women.
notes: Affirmation without mechanism: the essay cites the 1909 'Origin of Man' statement yet does not reproduce its 'begotten and born' language. The gap between what is cited and what is quoted is a precise measure of the reframe.

title: Dallin H. Oaks, October 2019 General Conference
speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
office: First Counselor in the First Presidency
summary: Cites 'the creative powers inherent in the combination of male and female' and quotes D&C 132's 'continuation of the seeds forever and ever' — the most explicit 21st-century General Conference reference, with the final noun left unstated.
transcription: [Verify exact talk and wording: 'the creative powers inherent in the combination of male and female — what modern revelation describes as the "continuation of the seeds forever and ever."']
notes: Borderline FORWARD-EXPLICIT: quoting D&C 132:19 in a marriage context does the doctrinal work while the sentence never says 'spirit children.' Confirm the exact talk title from the October 2019 sessions (likely the women's session address or 'Two Great Commandments') before publishing.

title: Camille N. Johnson, 'Lessons Learned in Inviting Christ to Author My Story'
speaker: Camille N. Johnson
summary: States that 'whether we are sealed and bear children in this life or the next, our object is exaltation' — a current official-magazine affirmation of posthumous childbearing.
transcription: ...whether we are sealed and bear children in this life or the next, our object is exaltation.
notes: A rare recent explicit: 'bear children... in the next [life]' asserts the forward mechanism in a 2025 correlated publication, against the general drift toward euphemism. Notable that it arrives in a pastoral context (comforting those without children in mortality) rather than a doctrinal exposition.
